summary: Initial discovery to map Thornfield's data residency and logging constraints across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment options. Main concerns: EU customer PII residency, audit log retention and redaction, KMS key residency/escrow, SOC2 obligations, and how Redwood's Dedicated or Private options support tenant isolation and legal hold. Agreed to follow up with security artifact pack and propose a Dedicated pilot for benchmarking.
topics: audit log retention and redaction policies
hosting fit: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC
tenant isolation, tenant ops and legal hold
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-08-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: 37 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Rafael Ortiz (Redwood Solutions Architect) -- Claire Nguyen (Thornfield Head of Security), Marcus Lee (CTO), Sophie Patel (Compliance), Aaron Mills (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): customer wants to understand which deployment mode meets EU PII residency, needs evidence for audits, wants detail on logs and redaction, K M S residency and whether private control plane is available.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, we'll do a quick rundown of why we're here — map constraints and figure out next steps. I'm Jordan, AE on this. Priya and Rafael are here to handle technical bits. Claire, Marcus — thanks for joining.

[00:18] Claire: Thanks, yes, short intro from our side, I'm Claire, Head of Security at Thornfield, responsible for audit evidence and vendor controls. Marcus is our CTO, Sophie handles compliance and Aaron is our infra lead.

[00:35] Marcus: Quick note, timeline: procurement wants a recommendation by end of August, so tight. We're evaluating Hosted, Dedicated, and Private/VPC options. Primary blocker is EU customer data and audit evidence.

[00:50] Priya: Great, we'll try to map that out. Can you outline the residency constraints? Are you seeing strict in-region processing, or more of a copy/retention restriction?

[01:04] Sophie: Good question. For EU customers we need both processing and storage to be in the EU for PII. We also have a right-to-be-forgotten flow where data needs to be deletable on request, and we need evidence. Retention windows differ by product — mortgage docs for 7 years, but derivative telemetry for 1 year.

[01:30] Aaron: Also, we have some downstream systems in the US that consume anonymized telemetry. So we need a clear separation and proof that raw PII never left EU.

[01:45] Rafael: Understood. On Redwood's side — hosted runs in our region-specific clusters, but if you need contractual region locking and keys held in your control plane we usually recommend Dedicated or Private. Hosted can be configured to only run in eu-west but contractually it's a bit more limited.

[02:10] Claire: About keys — KMS is a big one. We need either customer-managed keys where keys can't be exported, or H M S-backed keys with residency guarantees. Can Redwood support that?

[02:26] Priya: Yes, Dedicated supports customer-managed K M S keys and HSM integrations. Private/VPC gives you the most control, including local K M S and the option to hold keys in your cloud account. Hosted supports per-tenant encryption but with provider-managed keys by default.

[02:46] Marcus: So if we do Dedicated, can we ensure the keys never leave the EU? Like key residency?

[02:54] Rafael: Yes, Dedicated can be deployed into EU-only capacity and we can set up a K M S integration that uses your cloud K M S. For Private deployments we can put the control plane in your VPC and you retain full key control, which satisfies stricter K M S residency and escrow concerns.

[03:20] Claire: Audit logs — we need full request-level audit logs for three years for certain workflows, and they must be tamper-evident. Also, logs may contain PII so we need redaction or policy-based filter before any cross-border transfers. How does Redwood expose logs and what do they contain?

[03:40] Jordan: We expose request-level logs, model routes, token counts, and error traces. By default logs include prompts and responses, which could contain PII. Redwood has log redaction options and filters; on Dedicated and Private we can configure pre-ingest redaction and retention windows. For hosted we can do policy rules but contractual attestation for retention and deletion is more limited.

[04:10] Sophie: What does pre-ingest redaction look like? Is it a rule engine or do we need to handle it client-side?

[04:20] Priya: We offer both. You can do client-side masking before sending, or we can apply server-side transforms as a pre-ingest pipeline on Dedicated/Private — regex, PII detectors, or customer-provided transforms. There's also an option to never persist raw input (ephemeral-only processing) for certain endpoints.

[04:42] Aaron: Ephemeral-only processing — that would be great for verification flows. Does that impact latency or cost?

[04:48] Priya: Slightly, since ephemerality limits caching and batching optimizations. So there's a performance v cost tradeoff. For heavy throughput flows we usually recommend a hybrid: ephemeral for sensitive routes, cached for general purpose.

[05:06] Claire: Can Redwood provide a cryptographic proof or tamper-evidence for logs? We rely on append-only storage with checksums for some vendors.

[05:16] Rafael: We support WORM-style storage for logs on Dedicated and Private, and we can hash logs for tamper-evidence. For hosted, we can provide exportable logs and signed attestations, but the deep WORM storage is typically part of the Dedicated add-on.

[05:36] Marcus: Ok. Another question: legal hold — when litigation arises we might need to preserve certain records and not redact them for a time. Can redaction be reversible under an authorization flow?

[05:50] Sophie: Or at least we need a way to produce unredacted content to legal under strict controls.

[05:58] Priya: We have two patterns: (1) redaction with a reversible tokenization where original content is stored encrypted under your key (so accessible with proper authorizations), and (2) a purging-only pipeline where raw is never stored. Reversible tokenization is available on Dedicated/Private with customer K M S. Hosted is more restrictive on reversible patterns.

[06:22] Claire: That matches our needs — reversible tokenization with customer keys would work, provided key residency is guaranteed. Also need role-based access control so only legal can unseal.

[06:33] Jordan: RBAC is standard; Dedicated has tenant-level RBAC and audit trails for key unseal.

[06:42] Marcus: On the GDPR side — do you have documented assistance for subject access requests and right to be forgotten? We need an auditable flow demonstrating deletion across buckets and backups.

[06:55] Rafael: We provide deletion APIs and retention controls, and for Dedicated/Private we can evince deletion across the stack. We also provide guidance on backups and snapshots. For hosted, we provide support but the contractual guarantees are narrower.

[07:15] Aaron: Snapshots are a worry — do backups replicate outside region?

[07:20] Priya: Backups can be configured regionally. For Dedicated and Private we can enforce region-only backups. Hosted may use multi-region replication for availability unless contractually scoped otherwise.

[07:36] Sophie: We're also under financial services regulations — we need to show segregation for different legal entities and proof that logs for EU subsidiaries are not accessible by US ops. How do you handle operator access across regions?

[07:50] Jordan: Operator access is controlled — for Hosted our ops team has limited admin capabilities and access is audited. For Dedicated and Private you can control access via SSO and tie accounts to your identity provider. We also offer geofenced operator controls for Dedicated premium.

[08:10] Claire: Do you support SAML/SSO with SCIM provisioning and fine-grained roles? We need this to map to our access matrix.

[08:17] Rafael: Yes — SAML, OIDC, SCIM provisioning are supported. On Dedicated/Private you can lock admin roles to your IdP. Hosted supports SSO but provisioning nuance is better for Dedicated.

[08:34] Marcus: For the pilot — if we run a Dedicated pilot, can you provide a bill of materials for instance types, GPUs, and throughput targets? We want to validate latency and KV cache behavior for our longest sequences (mortgage docs + context).

[08:50] Priya: Absolutely. We'll take a perf profile: sequence lengths, QPS, NVMe/SSD needs, and recommend a baseline machine type. We'll also run benchmark scripts that measure cold-start, sustained throughput, and K V cache hit rates.

[09:06] Aaron: About inference determinism — if we do quantized models or smaller variants as fallback, how does Redwood guarantee semantic parity for decision-critical outputs?

[09:18] Priya: We do model variant rollouts and can A/B test. For decision-critical flows you can pin a model version and require fallback policies that are conservative. We also provide evaluation harnesses to check for regressions. Quantization can change outputs slightly; we recommend running your evals before rolling to quantized variants.

[09:42] Claire: Is there SLO-based routing if eu capacity is under pressure? We don't want PII to be routed to other regions as fallback.

[09:53] Jordan: Good callout. Routing policies can be strict — you can configure regional-only routing and fail closed if eu capacity is exhausted. Alternatively, you can fail open with anonymization. Redwood provides policy controls per route.

[10:10] Sophie: On evidence, can you supply artifacts like SOC2 cookie trail, network diagrams, deployment manifests, and signed attestations for audits?

[10:22] Jordan: Yes — we'll package SOC2 reports, network diagrams (for Dedicated/Private we can include topology), and attestations. We'll also include a runbook for legal hold and deletion proof.

[10:36] Marcus: About cost — Dedicated sounds like a safer bet but expensive. Can Redwood do reserved capacity or burst options? We need a model for cost predictability.

[10:48] Rafael: We offer reserved capacity and burst pools. Dedicated includes committed throughput options; we can size a baseline for cost predictability. Private has a different licensing model — platform fee plus infra. Hosted is pay-as-you-go but the compliance add-ons add to price.

[11:07] Aaron: Any concerns about vendor lock-in for Private vs Dedicated? We have to avoid long migration lock-ins.

[11:15] Priya: We support model exportability and standard inference formats. Private gives you the most portability because you control the control plane; Dedicated uses our runtime but models can be exported. We'll document migration steps.

[11:30] Claire: One operational concern — who has access to raw cached K V entries? We want assurance that caches don't contain persistent PII accessible to operator accounts.

[11:42] Rafael: K V caches are ephemeral, encrypted in memory, and we have strict policies around operator access. For Dedicated/Private we can enforce that K V cache stays in-process and not written to disk; for hosted there are safeguards but we recommend dedicated if you need strict cache guarantees.

[11:58] Sophie: Let's scope the logs format — we need to be able to ingest them into our SIEM with fields: tenant_id, request_id, region, route, and retention TTL. Can you export in JSON with transport to our S3?

[12:12] Jordan: Yes, we can stream logs to your S3 (or to a secure syslog/Kinesis) and format them as JSON with the fields you listed. For Dedicated we can also do direct SIEM connectors.

[12:28] Marcus: Are there any known compliance blockers for the workflows we described (eu-only, reversible tokenization, tamper-evident logs)?

[12:36] Priya: Not blockers — more implementation work. Dedicated/Private map cleanly to those requirements. Hosted may need contractual extensions and might not satisfy the strictest key-residency or reversible tokenization guarantees.

[12:50] Claire: How about legal hold export — do you provide an immutable export package with manifests that we can hand to legal counsel?

[12:58] Rafael: Yes, we can produce an export bundle with manifests, hash lists, and chain-of-custody notes for any preserved data. That's typically part of the evidence pack for Dedicated.

[13:12] Aaron: If we decide Hosted for non-PII routes and Dedicated for PII routes, is routing and policy enforcement at the application layer or can Redwood split at the route level?

[13:24] Priya: We support per-route policies, so you can direct sensitive routes to Dedicated or Private backends while sending non-sensitive traffic to Hosted. The routing is policy-driven in the control plane.

[13:38] Marcus: Ok that's promising. Next steps then?

[13:44] Jordan: From Redwood: we'll send the security and evidence pack, propose a Dedicated pilot BOM and pricing, and schedule a legal deep-dive. From Thornfield: provide the control mapping and retention windows and confirm procurement timeline.

[13:58] Sophie: We'll do that; Claire will lead the control mapping. Procurement timeline is aiming end of August but may slide a week.

[14:08] Claire: A couple of nitty-gritty Qs — do you support customer managed key escrow for legal/regulatory reasons? We might need an escrow process.

[14:18] Rafael: We can support key escrow workflows via H M S and third-party escrow partners; that's usually part of a Private deployment negotiation. We'll include options in the pack.

[14:30] Aaron: Also, can we configure synthetic-data or prompt-sanitizer service to minimize sending PII upstream?

[14:37] Priya: Yes — we have a sanitizer service pattern and can deploy it as a pre-ingest lambda-style transform or as a client library. We'll include recommended patterns.

[14:50] Marcus: Any red flags we should be aware of when presenting this to our board?

[14:55] Jordan: The main board concerns are cost predictability and auditability. We'll provide a clear cost model for Dedicated pilot and a compliance artifacts checklist so you can present it to legal/audit.

[15:06] Sophie: Great. End-of-call recap?

[15:10] Jordan: Recap: Redwood to send security pack and SOC2, propose Dedicated pilot with BOM and benchmarking script, schedule compliance deep dive, provide routing and redaction options. Thornfield to send control map, retention windows, and procurement timeline.

[15:24] Claire: Confirmed. Looking forward to artifacts.

[15:30] Marcus: Thanks everyone.

[15:32] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up. Bye.

(End of meeting)
